ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A power supply and a resistance box are connected to form a closed circuit, and the curve of the power P consumed by the resistance box changing with the resistance-box reading R is measured as shown in Figure 9. From this it can be known that ( )

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The vertical axis in the attached figure is labeled P/W, and the horizontal axis is labeled R/Ω. The curve starts from the origin near R=0 and rises as R increases, reaching the highest point at R=5 Ω; in the figure, a vertical dashed line marks the R=5 Ω corresponding to this peak value, and a horizontal dashed line marks the peak power as about 45 W. After that, the curve decreases as R continues to increase. Then reason: The resistance-box reading R is the external resistance. When the electromotive force of the power supply is E and the internal resistance is r, the power consumed by the external resistance is P=I^2R=(E/(R+r))^2R=E^2R/(R+r)^2. For a fixed power supply, when the external resistance obtains the maximum power, it satisfies R=r, that is, the maximum power transfer condition. The image shows that the maximum power occurs at R=5 Ω, so the internal resistance r of the power supply must be equal to 5 Ω.
